# Lanternfield Trust Community Facilities Fund: Guidance for Applicants 2026

The Lanternfield Trust's guidance for its capital fund for community buildings and sports facilities, the 2026 edition. Downloaded from the trust's applicant portal on 2 March 2026; the PDF is in the club's shared drive under Facilities/Changing rooms/Grant.

## Summary

The fund makes capital grants of £50,000 to £200,000 to community organisations for new or improved buildings that are open to the public or to a membership drawn from the local community. It pays up to 75% of eligible project costs; the rest must come from match funding, which can include the applicant's own reserves and other grants but not volunteer time. There are two rounds a year.

## Key Details

- Grant size: £50,000 to £200,000.
- Intervention rate: up to 75% of eligible costs. Professional fees and a contingency of up to 10% are eligible; VAT is eligible only where it cannot be recovered.
- Security of tenure: the applicant must own the site or hold a lease with at least 25 years left to run from the date of the grant offer. A heads of terms is not enough on its own; the trust accepts a signed lease, or a resolution of the landlord's decision-making body committing to grant the lease, with the lease signed before the first payment.
- Match funding: must be secured or credibly pledged at application, with a statement of sources. Appeals count as pledged if the applicant shows a realistic plan and progress.
- Rounds in 2026-27: round 2 of 2026 closes 30 September 2026 with decisions in February 2027; round 1 of 2027 closes 31 March 2027 with decisions in July 2027.
- Assessment: need and demand, community benefit including safeguarding and access, deliverability (design, costs, procurement, project management), sustainability (running costs and maintenance plan), and value for money.
- Procurement: at least three written quotes for works over £100,000.
- Monitoring: an annual usage report for five years after completion, and a charge or restriction on the lease for 25 years in favour of the trust.

## Why It Matters

This is the document the whole [[new-changing-rooms]] project is built round. Our ask of £185,000 is 74.6% of the £248,000 cost, deliberately just under the 75% ceiling, and the other £63,000 is the [[match-funding]].

The tenure rule is why [[pitch-lease-extension]] exists at all: our lease ends on 31 March 2031, which gives less than five years. When I read the guidance in March 2026 I went through it with Marek and Claire and we marked three things as risks: tenure, the three-quote rule (done in June, [[changing-rooms-quote-comparison]]), and the maintenance plan, which we have only sketched ([[who-maintains-the-new-changing-rooms]]).

Esther Lowell later confirmed by email that a cabinet resolution would count as evidence ([[lanternfield-tenure-deadline-email-2026-10-09]]). That is what we are waiting for on 19 November.

## Caveats

- The guidance says the trust may change rounds and deadlines; check the portal before each submission.
- The 25-year charge on the lease will need the council's consent as landlord. Graham Sutcliffe has said this is normal but it is not yet written into the heads of terms.
